Details.JobSummary: About the position: This position is Non-appropriated Fund (NAF) and will be assigned to the Marketing at Barksdale AFB, LA Full-Time position with 20 Hours Guaranteed Hours and Benefits
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Thank you for considering employment with Air Force Services Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF).
MajorDuties: Works with the Marketing Director to develop and implement marketing, publicity, graphics, and media activities for the 2nd Force Support Squadron. Position is under the direct supervision of the Marketing Director. Responsible for graphic design and print operations for the marketing department at 2nd Force Support Squadron, Barksdale AFB. Develops original designs, concepts or visual styles for promotional materials, web pages, social media content, on-base advertisements, and other media. Designs must follow branding guidelines and clearly convey 2 FSS message. Executes designs and layouts using the Adobe Creative Suite with proficiency, with an emphasis on Adobe Photoshop, as well as Illustrator, InDesign and other creative platforms. Collaborates with web and social media public affairs assistant in content creation and strategy planning for, and the maintenance of, 2 FSS website and FSS social media platforms. Works with activity managers and other stakeholders on the design of effective advertising vehicles and appropriate media mixes. Obtains information on upcoming events, special programs, and offers, to create effective promotional materials. To include dates, times and locations are correct and verified. Communicates via email, phone or through the work order system with activity managers about changes, additions, or design of products. Ensures proper layout of all designs for effective printing and cutting, to include setting accurate dimensions and bleed areas. Creates physical marketing pieces, to include posters, flyers, brochures, banners, and more; operates equipment such as printers, laminators, mounters, folders, cutters, etc., safely and effectively. Maintains specialized equipment to ensure it is in working order and reports need for repair or purchase to supervisor. Performs other duties assigned by Marketing Director. If interested in applying for this position you may preview the online application: https://apply.usastaffing.gov/ViewQuestionnaire/12810254

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To qualify for a Public Affairs Specialist your resume and supporting documentation must support: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience that equipped you with the particular competencies to successfully perform the duties of the position and is directly in or related to this position. To qualify at the GS-13 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military, or private sector. Applicants must meet eligibility requirements including time-in-grade (General Schedule (GS) positions only), time-after-competitive appointment, minimum qualifications, and any other regulatory requirements by the cut- off/closing date of the announcement. Creditable specialized experience includes: Plans, creates, designs, executes, and disseminates informational materials and products that communicate to both a worldwide internal organizational audience and a worldwide base of organizational customers and interested publics. Facilitates publishing content to organization websites and works with developers and operations staff to assess and resolve any technical challenges in displaying the content. Develops internal information campaigns, and researches and writes information materials appropriate for both internal and external release. Interviews sources and research references to write articles for publication that promote organization and items of command interest. Edits articles to ensure consistency with command policy, correctness of grammar and spelling, and readability. Verifies information to ensure accuracy. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Nation's Logistics Combat Support Agency: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is a U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) agency. DLA provides worldwide logistics support for the missions of the Military Departments and the Unified Combatant Commands under conditions of peace and war. It also provides logistics support to other DoD Components and certain Federal agencies, foreign governments, international organizations, and others as authorized.

To be well-qualified and exercise selection priority for this vacancy, displaced Federal employees must be rated at a score of 85 or higher for this position. ICTAP eligibles must submit one of the following as proof of eligibility for the special selection priority: a separation notice; a "Notice of Personnel Action" (SF-50) documenting separation; an agency certification that you cannot be placed after injury compensation has been terminated; an OPM notification that your disability annuity has been terminated; OR a Military Department or National Guard Bureau notification that you are retired under 5 U.S.C. 8337(h) or 8456. NOTE: Previous federal employees must also submit the following additional documentation: SF-50s (e.g., LWOP, highest grade held, overseas appointments, etc.), SF-75 information, and documentation of performance rating of record (dated within the last 12 months). Selected PPP MSP applicants will need to certify they have not accepted nor declined another offer of permanent, Federal employment (to include NAF and the military exchange services) since relocating to the military sponsor's current duty station. Priority Placement Program (PPP) DoD Retained Grade Preference (RGP): In order to receive this preference, you must choose to apply using the "Priority Placement Program, DoD Retained Grade Preference (RGP)" eligibility. If you are claiming RGP and are determined to be Well Qualified (score of 85 or above) for the position, you will be referred to the hiring manager as a priority applicant. Information and required documentation for claiming RGP may be found at the General Applicant Information and Definitions link below. To be eligible as a RGP, you must submit the following supporting documents with your application package: a signed Retained Grade PPP Self-Certification Checklist (DD3145-1 (whs.mil)); a copy of your Notification of Personnel Action (SF-50) effecting the placement in retained grade status; or a copy of the notification letter you received regarding the RIF or classification downgrade.

As of 23 December 2016, Military retirees seeking to enter federal service in the Department of Defense now require a waiver if they would be appointed within 180 days following their official date of retirement. Drug-Free Workplace Policy The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is committed to maintaining a safe, drug-free workplace. All DLA employees are required to refrain from illegal drug use on and off duty. DLA conducts pre-employment, reasonable suspicion, post-accident, and random drug testing. Applicants tentatively selected for employment in testing designated positions will undergo a urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Refusal to undergo testing or testing positive for illegal drugs will result in withdrawal of the tentative job offer and a six-month denial of employment with DLA from the date of the drug test. Employees in drug testing designated positions are subject to random drug testing. The DLA drug testing panel tests for the following substances: marijuana, cocaine, opiates, heroin, phencyclidine, amphetamines, methamphetamines, fentanyl, norfentanyl, methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), and opioids. ADVISORY: Use of cannabidiol (CBD) products may result in a positive drug test for marijuana. DLA employees are subject to Federal law and under Federal law, Marijuana is a Schedule I drug and is illegal.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: DoDEA Americas Southeast District operates 24 schools in 4 states across 2 time zones. The Fort Benning Schools are part of the DoDEA Americas Southeast District. We have a total of 5 schools to serve military connected students in PK through grade 8. Salary based on Full-time work schedule, this position is Part-time/Seasonal 70 hours per pay period.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Department of Defense Education Activity (DoDEA), as one of only two Federally-operated school systems, is responsible for planning, directing, coordinating, and managing prekindergarten through 12th grade educational programs on behalf of the Department of Defense (DoD). DoDEA is globally positioned, operating 160 accredited schools in 8 districts located in 11 foreign countries, 7 states, Guam, and Puerto Rico. DoDEA employs approximately 15,000 employees who serve more than 72,000 children of active duty military and DoD civilian families. DoDEA is committed to ensuring that all school-aged children of military families are provided a world-class education that prepares them for postsecondary education and/or career success and to be leading contributors in their communities as well as in our 21st century globalized society.
MajorDuties: Serve as an interpreter for deaf and/or hearing impaired students.
Interprets teacher's directions and messages in sign language to students.
Provide supervision of and instruction to students on simple subject matter.
Clearly explain concepts being taught and observe students for understanding.
Develop audio-visual tactile aides and set up lab demonstrations.
Distribute and collect testing materials as needed by students.
Supervises student meal and play times.

Details.JobSummary: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. This National Guard position is for a PUBLIC AFFAIRS SPECIALIST, Position Description Number D1167000 and is part of the NCNG PAO, National Guard (JFHQ - PAO /Manning Doc 1212-403). POSITION MAY BE SUBJECT TO NIGHT SHIFT WORK ADDITIONAL TO WEEKENDS.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community!
MajorDuties: As a PUBLIC AFFAIRS SPECIALIST, GS-1035-09, you will develop news releases and feature articles describing Guard sponsored activities or events, presentation ceremonies, etc; distribute these to local and national print and broadcast media representatives; respond orally and in writing to requests for information from Guard members, member associations, external audiences or special interest groups; determine the sensitivity of data requested and if data is determined to be sensitive or controversial; coordinate data release with a senior Public Affairs (PA) Specialist; evaluate local media programming on NG events, activities or communication campaigns to identify potential public relation issues with message content or format; once identified, advises management on potential causes of the problem and forwards suggestions for resolving them; gather data on public reaction to communication campaigns for analyses and evaluation; when the evaluation is completed, draws the appropriate conclusions and from these develops and submits recommendations to the PAO for improving the campaign's appeal to the general public or target audience; prepare and disseminate news releases and feature articles to the media for print. Selects and incorporates photographs, film footage, etc., into the release or article to visually enhance the message with viewers; consult with the pertinent program specialist to obtain the latest information for use in news releases, radio spots, print articles, meetings and electronic broadcasts; develop semi-technical written materials to educate a specific audience on the nature and purpose of the NG's programs, policies and practices; develop positive working relationships with state and local government personnel, community or special interest groups or individuals desiring input on state level NG policy, practices or programs; other duties as assigned. POSITION MAY BE SUBJECT TO NIGHT SHIFT WORK ADDITIONAL TO WEEKENDS.

Details.JobSummary: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. This National Guard position is for a VISUAL INFORMATION SPECIALIST (TITLE 32), Position Description Number D159000 and is part of the NCNG PAO, National Guard (JFHQ- PAO / MD 1224/055). POSITION MAY BE SUBJECT TO NIGHT SHIFT WORK ADDITIONAL TO WEEKENDS.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community!
MajorDuties: As a VISUAL INFORMATION SPECIALIST, GS-1084-11, you will plan and administer the state's VI program; oversee the development of immediate and long-term plans; develop policies, directives, and standard operating procedures (SOP); manage the state's VI architecture, ensuring all changes are properly documented; maintain close liaison with Department of Army, Department of Air Force, National Guard Bureau (NGB), federal and state agencies, business leaders, joint staff and operational personnel to ensure efficient VI operations; forecast and execute the state's VI budget, to include procurement of equipment and supplies; coordinate all activities related to the full range of VI products and services for the state such as still photography (photo-chemical and digital video), manual and computer-generated graphics, presentation services (conference rooms and classrooms), VI equipment and product loan, video(acquisition, production, post-production and duplication), audio (production and duplication), video teleconferencing, closed circuit television, and master antenna and cable television; coordinate with various outside agencies/contractors on projects that may involve research, procurement and installation of contract services; direct design of unique projects from inception to completion through application of innovative solutions in the use of multimedia technologies; accept or reject customer produced or procured materials; analyze statistical information, personnel data, or general descriptions of information to be visually depicted; select appropriate visual media for the project that will best represent the information to be presented; manage production of electronic and printed material in the form of slides, displays, newsletters, pamphlets, web pages, posters, and leaflets for various activities; direct page layouts allowing for line art, photographs, graphs and other graphics; provide higher-level management with VI products, services, consultation, facilities (studio or presentation room) and equipment to support functional areas, to include command and control, training, logistics, medical, personnel, special operations, engineering, and public affairs; manage the state's Visual Information Support Center; responsible for training and coordinating equipment usage; manage stock videos, audio computer graphics, slides, photographs, line drawings and hardcopy clip art libraries (to include manuals, CD ROMs, videotapes, videodisks); maintain the state's defense visual information activity number (DVIAN) account; coordinate VI usage logs and submits required reports; manage the installation, set up, and technical support of the state's Distributed Training Technology (DTT)/Distance Learning Network (DLN); serve as a member of the state DTT/DLN Advisory Board. Plan, design, develop, test, implement, and manage the Internet, Intranet, and Extranet activities, including systems/applications development and technical management of web sites; interface with all state staff offices and units to collect files, data, publications, and current information, in an electronic format, to consolidate, organize and create interactive web pages with necessary hypertext links to produce accessible "online" information; manage Internet server operations through continuous maintenance and updates of information as dictated by the staff offices and units; work with the functional proponents of databases to convert those databases to interactive HTML web page files; assist staff offices and units with technical advice and information for efficient data transmission into web pages; ensure all material presented is in compliance with copyright requirements and that Web design is in compliance with Americans with Disabilities Act for accessibility; work with the Data Base Manager to develop interactive databases for applications on the web; and perform other duties as assigned. POSITION MAY BE SUBJECT TO NIGHT SHIFT WORK ADDITIONAL TO WEEKENDS.

A qualified candidate must possess: Broad and in-depth knowledge of the goals, principles and techniques of the administration, management, marketing and financial processes of a large business, community, industrial or military community support program. Knowledge of the application of a wide range of quantitative and qualitative methods for the assessment and improvement of complex management programs and systems. Knowledge of desktop publishing, content management systems, graphic design, digital photography, and video software programs, and other software programs, to be able to prepare or coordinate the production of marketing products, including print and audiovisual products, social media tools and websites, and other promotional products such as advertisements and exhibits. Mastery knowledge of communication principles, methods, practices and techniques, analytical methods, and interpersonal relations practices sufficient to develop and apply new approaches to the most difficult and complex problems by developing or evaluating information programs enhancing understanding Ability to lead collaboratively, motivate and inspire teamwork, to influence senior leadership and guide subordinates. Understanding of the chain of command and how to utilize it effectively. High degree of proficiency, skill, and knowledge with computer programs including desktop publishing, Power Point, Word, Excel, Access and other business applications. Must have high proficiency in the management of website development, print industry processes, electronic media, and social media. Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the expertise to compose correspondence, including writing and editing documents and publications that encompass all Regional Fleet & Family Readiness Programs' operational, administrative, and financial matters, or similar business, community, industrial or military community support programs, Skilled in developing budgets and evaluating effectiveness and viability. Skilled in keeping projects on track and managing task efficiently while working with cross functional teams. Ability to fully exercise all delegated supervisory and managerial authority possible with responsibility for accomplishing the designated mission. Ability to supervise and direct work of other employees, monitor performance, and ensure that adequate internal control procedures are developed and operative. Ability to negotiate, author and execute commercial sponsorship solicitations as well as after-action reports.

Details.JobSummary: Position assigned to the NAF Marketing Branch N94P; Fleet and Family Readiness Support Services, N94; Navy Region Mid-Atlantic. Incumbent is responsible for overall planning, initiation, management, administration and technical direction of comprehensive communications, marketing, and commercial sponsorship and advertising programs for FFR Programs; incumbent serves as division head for Marketing N94P. RESUMES WILL BE REVIEWED AT FIRST CUT OFF DATE OF 13 OCTOBER 2025
Details.SubAgencyName: CNRMA-COMMERCIAL ACTIVITIES MARKETING JEB LITTLE CREEK VIRGINIA BEACH, VA N92
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: CNIC offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. CNIC provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. The mission of the Fleet and Family Readiness (FFR) Programs is to maximize the physical, emotional and social development of the fleet, fighter and family. FFR enables a ready Navy force through its Fleet Readiness, Family Readiness, and Housing Programs. We provide direct and support services to all non-appropriated fund (NAF) employees who work for Morale, Welfare and Recreation (MWR), and Navy Getaways throughout the FFR Program worldwide.
MajorDuties: Duties include but are not limited to: Marketing and Communications 40% Serves as the principal advisor to the Regional FFR Program Director and Regional Program Managers in all matters pertaining to communications and marketing policies and services. Incumbent is responsible for developing long-term marketing and strategic plans to maximize patron utilization and satisfaction while enhancing FFR member programs' self-sufficiency and/or profitability. Identifies, on a continuing basis, areas for potential improvement in the promotion and operation of FFR programs, including opportunities for controlling costs and/or realizing increased revenues through new ventures and expanded services. Has authority to represent FFR Programs at meetings and conferences pertaining to programs, policies, operations and support functions. Hosts meetings and conferences to communicate and discuss matters of similar content of importance to Program Managers, site managers and outlying base marketing staff. Directs the overall management and coordination of a progressive and complex marketing and graphics division, sign/banner production and print shop operation. Responsible for the production of all marketing materials from inception to completion through supervision of design, composition, printing, production, distribution, and accuracy of graphic arts services and written communications for FFR programs to include, but not limited to, Web sites, Social Media, digital signage, direct mail magazines, all forms of printed media, signs, banners, paid advertising, press releases, public service announcements, broadcast and print media advertising, photography, and video. Directs the overall management and coordination of electronic media including, but not limited to, briefs and other presentations, websites, on-base marquees, and electronic newsletters. Serves as Regional N9 Webmaster with responsibility for content, compliance and efficacy of all Web sites and Web pages representing N9 programs. Continuously evaluates and reviews program and campaign strategies based on patron utilization, resources, needs assessments, program objectives and funding considerations. Conducts market research, studies, and focus groups. Serves as the FFR Regional liaison to Regional and Installation Public Affairs Offices. Serves as FFR spokesperson and primary point of contact for media and outside organizations. Responsible for providing full visibility and dissemination of information for all FFR programs through written communications, presentations, speeches, military messages, press releases, and other means available. Commercial Sponsorship and Advertising 35% Responsible for the oversight and execution of all aspects of the MWR Commercial Sponsorship and Advertising Program for the region to include, but not limited to, developing strategy, matching target populations and events with potential corporate sponsors, costing events, determining opportunities for sponsors and advertisers, pricing sponsorships and advertising media, soliciting sponsorship, developing proposal packages, overseeing the preparation of and approving sponsorship contracts. Serves as Regional NAF Air Show/Open House Coordinator supporting both Regional and Installation commands in planning, funding and producing Base open house events. Supervisory 25% Directly supervises a Regional Marketing Department which provides all marketing services to installations within Navy Region Mid-Atlantic and edits, designs and produces marketing materials. Direct reports may include but are not limited to a Regional Supervisory Commercial Sponsorship Coordinator (NF-4), Sponsorship coordinators (NF-3), Marketing Specialists (NF-3), Visual Information Specialists (NF-3), Marketing Assistant (NF-2) and Print Production Coordinator (NF-3). Plans regular work assignments for direct reports; prepares plans to meet substantial changes in workload; justifies revisions in staffing levels, work priorities, and deadlines. Assigns work to employees based on selective considerations of such factors as the difficulty and requirements of assignments; availability, capability, and special qualifications of employees; and workload. Develops and issues written instructions and standard operating procedures and ensures compliance. Reviews work and accept or rejects products; provides guidance on remedial actions needed. Supports CNIC's Equal Employment Opportunities (EEO) policy; fosters a work environment free of discrimination, harassment, and/or reprisal; ensures all subordinate staff understands and adheres to policy; and ensures the treatment of all staff is fair and equitable.
Details.Education: Masters in Business Administration with concentration in marketing/communications) and specialized certifications (digital marketing, content marketing, strategic communication) is preferred, but not required.
